questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: Given the matrix \[\begin{bmatrix} -4&2 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\], the eigenvector is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} A &=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-4 & 2 \\4 & 3\end{array}\right] \\ |A-\lambda I|&= 0 \\ -4 \quad 2|-| \begin{array}{cc}\lambda & 3\end{array}|-\lambda|&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \left|\begin{array}{cc}-4-\lambda & 2 \\4 & 3-\lambda\end{array}\right| &=0 \\ (-4-\lambda)(3-\lambda)-8 &=0 \\ -12+4 \lambda-3 \lambda+\lambda^{2}-8 &=0 \\ \lambda^{2}+\lambda-20 &=0 \\ (\lambda+5)(\lambda-4) &=0 \\ \lambda &=-5,4 \end{aligned}\]
Let, eigen vector be \[\left[\begin{array}{l}m_{1}\\m_{2}\end{array}\right];\] Putting, \(\lambda_{1}=-5\)
\[\begin{aligned} \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 2 \\4 & 8\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}m_{1} \\m_{2}\end{array}\right]&=0 \\ \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 2 \\1 & 2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}m_{1} \\m_{2}\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{l}0 \\0\end{array}\right]\\ \Rightarrow\quad\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}m_{1} \\ m_{2}\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{l}0 \\ 0\end{array}\right] \\ m_{1}+2 m_{2}&=0 \end{aligned}\]
Taking the value, \(m_{1}=2\) and \(m_{2}=-1\)
thus the eigen vector correspondence to eigen value \[\lambda_{1}=-5 \text{ is } X_{1}=\left[\begin{array}{c}2 \\ -1\end{array}\right]\]

questions.question: The value of the integral \(I=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}\int_{0}^{\infty }exp(-\frac{x^{2}}{8})dx\) is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} \quad I&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-x^{2} / 8} d x \\ \text { Put } \quad \frac{x^{2}}{8}&= t \Rightarrow x^{2}=8 t \\ \Rightarrow \quad x &=2 \sqrt{2 t} \\ \therefore \quad d x &=4 \frac{d t}{x}=\frac{4}{2 \sqrt{2}} \frac{d t}{\sqrt{t}} \\ \text { or } \quad d x&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{t}} d t \\ I &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-t} \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{t}} d t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-t} t^{\frac{1}{2}-1} d t \\ \quad &\left[\because \sqrt{n}=\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-x} x^{n-1} d x \text { and }\left[\frac{1}{2}=\sqrt{\pi}\right]\right.\\ \therefore \quad I=& \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \cdot \sqrt{\pi}=1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
The output y(t) of a linear time invariant system is related to its input x(t) by the following equations:
\(y(t)=0.5x(t-t_{d}+T)+x(t-t_{d})\) \(+0.5x(t-t_{d}+T)\)
The filter transfer function H(\(\omega\)) of such a system is given by
questions.explanation:
\(y(t)=0.5 x\left(t-t_{d}+T\right)+0.5 x\left(t-t_{d}-T\right)+x\left(t-t_{d}\right)\)
Taking Fourier transform
\[\begin{aligned} Y(\omega)&=\left[0.5 e^{j \omega\left(-t_{d}+T\right)}+0.5 e^{j \omega\left(-t_{d}+T \right)}+e^{-j \omega t_{d}}\right] X(\omega) \\ \frac{Y(\omega)}{X(\omega)}&=e^{-j \omega t_{d}}\left[0.5 e^{j \omega T}+0.5 e^{-j\omega T}+1\right] \\ \frac{Y(\omega)}{X(\omega)}&=e^{-j \omega t} [\cos \omega T+1] \\ H(\omega)&=(1+\cos \omega T) e^{-j \omega t_d} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: A signal \(x(n)=sin(\omega _{0}n+\phi )\) is the input to a linear time- invariant system having a frequency response H(\(e^{j\omega }\)). If the output of the system Ax(n - \(n_{0}\)) then the most general form of \(\angle H(e^{j\omega })\) will be

For break away and break in point
\[\begin{array}{l} \quad \frac{d K}{d s}=(1-s)(2 s+3)+s^{2}+3 s=0 \\ =-s^{2}+2 s+3=0 \\ \Rightarrow s^{2}-2 s-3=0 \\ \Rightarrow(s-3)(s+1)=0 \\ s=3,-1 \end{array}\]
-1 is the breakaway point and 3 is the break in point.

\[\begin{aligned} F(z)&=\frac{1}{2} z+1+2 z^{-1}+z^{-2}+\frac{1}{2} z^{-3} \\ Z &=e^{j \omega} \\ F\left(e^{j \omega}\right) &=\frac{1}{2} e^{j \omega}+1+2 e^{-j \omega}+e^{-2 j \omega}+\frac{1}{2} e^{-3 j \omega} \\ &=e^{-j \omega}\left(\frac{1}{2} e^{2 j \omega}+e^{j \omega}+2+e^{-j \omega}+\frac{1}{2} e^{-2 j \omega}\right) \\ &=e^{-j \omega\left[\frac{e^{2 j \omega}+e^{-2 j \omega}}{2}+e^{j \omega}+e^{-j \omega}+2\right]} \\ f(n) &=e^{-j \omega}[\cos 2 \omega+2 \cos \omega+2] \end{aligned}\]
